retained_skill: Debugging a C image-processing program by tracing incorrect spatial-filter behavior and memory errors, then repairing blur, Sobel, boundary, initialization, and parser defects.
bottleneck: The public request allows conventional grayscale conversions, but the verifier requires one unstated coefficient set and also bakes that set into its Sobel expectation. All 12 attempts left a reasonable weighted grayscale implementation in place; even the two attempts that repaired the remaining spatial and memory defects were rejected only at those two coupled checks.
change: Repair in the grading contract: state that a conventional RGB-to-grayscale weighting may be chosen if edge detection uses it consistently, and grade grayscale semantics plus Sobel behavior relative to the program's own grayscale result. This removes the hidden coefficient choice without supplying any of the retained debugging decisions.
restore: A later variant can require a named grayscale standard in the public instruction and restore a single exact coefficient-based expectation; it must not silently restore an unstated formula.
prediction: Attempts currently stop after fixing observable crashes and spatial-filter defects because their reasonable grayscale weighting still receives two failures. Removing the hidden coefficient requirement lets attempts that also correct the Sobel sign, such as attempt-04, submit a passing result; this is refuted if replaying attempt-04 still fails any retained check or if nearly every future attempt passes despite most current attempts omitting the Sobel correction.
